title: Hagia Sophia
summary: Built in about six years for the Byzantine emperor Justinian I, Hagia Sophia has been a church, a mosque, a museum and a mosque again.
description: An earlier church on the site burned during the Nika insurrection of January 532, giving Justinian I the opportunity to build a splendid replacement. The new Hagia Sophia was completed in 537, designed by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidorus of Miletus, architects known for their knowledge of mechanics and mathematics.
Over the centuries it served as an Eastern Orthodox church, a Roman Catholic cathedral (1204–61), an Orthodox church again, a mosque from 1453, a museum from 1935, and again a mosque from 2020.
context: Hagia Sophia became a model for a whole family of later churches and mosques. It is part of the Historic Areas of Istanbul, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.

facts.text: It was built between 532 and 537 CE under Justinian I.
Its architects were Anthemius of Tralles and Isidorus of Miletus.
It was a mosque from 1453 to 1935, a museum from 1935 to 2020, and has been a mosque again since 2020.
